decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Owen' in turn 1, establishing B's name explicitly.
A's definite possessive 'your family vacation' presupposes B has a family vacation.

'Didn't you bring his favorite toy?' presupposes a male child for whom B is responsible (bringing toy, family vacation context). Well-grounded inference that B has a child, though not strictly guaranteed (could be nephew).
decisions.counterexample: B could be bringing a toy for a nephew or other relative's child on the family vacation.

decisions.reason: A explicitly states 'You've got a beautiful tan' directly about B.
'Where did you go?' presupposes B went to a destination.

decisions.claim: B must have had a great time
decisions.reason: This is A's opinion/inference about B's experience, not a factual attribute of B. B could have had a mediocre or bad time despite the tan and vacation.
decisions.counterexample: B went on vacation, got a tan, but had a stressful or boring time.

decisions.reason: 'His friends will be very happy' presupposes the male child has friends.
'get the little souvenir' presupposes B obtained/has a souvenir to give.
'B has a family' is entailed by 'your family vacation' (c2), which already captures the family vacation including the family presupposition.

decisions.claim: B went on a family vacation
decisions.reason: 'B went on a family vacation' is equivalent to c2 'B has a family vacation' combined with c5 'B went somewhere.' The family vacation presupposition is already in c2.

decisions.claim: B brought a male child's favorite toy
decisions.reason: This is essentially c3 restated with the additional detail about bringing the toy. c3 already establishes B has a male child; the 'bringing' aspect is a question, not a confirmed action.

decisions.claim: There is a male child associated with B who has a favorite toy
decisions.reason: This is a rephrasing of c3's core claim: there is a male child associated with B who has a favorite toy. c3 already captures this.

decisions.claim: B has a souvenir to give to the child's friends
decisions.reason: c8 already states B obtained a souvenir. c13 adds 'to give to the child's friends' which is also captured by c7's context. These refer to the same event.
c7 already states 'B's child has friends.' c14 says 'The male child has friends' — same fact at same granularity.

decisions.claim: The vacation involved a beach or sandy location
decisions.reason: A's turn 7 says 'Most children love to play in the sand on the beach' — this is a general statement about what children like, not a claim that B's vacation was at a beach. A is making a generic observation, not confirming B's destination.
decisions.counterexample: B went to a mountain or lake vacation; A is simply making a general remark about children and beaches.

decisions.reason: A explicitly describes the souvenir as 'little,' establishing its size.
